summary.text: Allan Doensen is a One Nation candidate for the Western Metropolitan Region in the Legislative Council at the 2026 Victorian election, according to the party's candidate page; no source gives his place on the ticket. That page refused this tracker's automated requests when this profile was researched, and no other source had published a biography of him as at early November 2026.
summary.note: The tracker recorded his endorsement from the party's page earlier in November 2026, but the page blocked our script when this profile was researched, so it could not be read again.

summary.text: Anneke Demanuele leads the Victorian Socialists' ticket for Western Metropolitan Region in the 2026 Legislative Council election, with Jorge Jorquera second. On her party page she says she rents in Maribyrnong, grew up in a working-class family in a regional area and joined the socialist movement in 2014. She writes that she has helped organise protests for refugee rights, against far-right groups and, in 2020, a large march during the bushfire crisis.

lives.note: She says she is a renter in Maribyrnong, which could mean the suburb or the wider City of Maribyrnong.

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia lists a Victorian Socialists candidate named Anneke Demanuele; same name and party, but no source we read says it is her.

summary.text: Brittney Henderson, a Wiradjuri and Bunurong person raised in Melbourne's west, leads the Greens' ticket for Western Metropolitan Region in the 2026 Legislative Council election. Henderson's work has been with Aboriginal community-controlled organisations and other not-for-profit groups; Henderson also chairs Deadly Sports Plus, an Aboriginal-led first aid and training service, and worked on the Greens' 2025 federal campaign in Fraser.

summary.text: Moira Deeming has represented Western Metropolitan Region in the Legislative Council since 2022, when she was elected as a Liberal; she is a former teacher and Melton councillor. In 2023 she was suspended and then expelled from the Liberal party room after a dispute with then leader John Pesutto over a rally she co-organised, and she was readmitted in December 2024 after the Federal Court found Pesutto had defamed her. The Liberals revoked her endorsement for the 2026 election in July 2026, she left the parliamentary party later that month and sat as an independent, and in September 2026 she joined Family First. She heads Family First's ticket for Western Metropolitan in 2026.

prior_roles.note: Elected as a Liberal. Parliament records her as Liberal until late July 2026, Independent until early September 2026 and Family First since; Wikipedia dates her announcement that she was joining Family First a few days later in September 2026, and adds that she sat as an Independent Liberal while outside the Liberal party room in 2023-24.

prior_roles.role: Shadow Assistant Minister for Local Government
Liberal Party Whip in the Legislative Council

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia doesn't say what label she stood under at this council election; the code is her party at the time.

legal_and_integrity.text: The Liberal party room suspended her for nine months in March 2023 over a rally she helped organise, then expelled her.
legal_and_integrity.outcome: Expelled by a party-room vote of 19 to 11 in May 2023; readmitted in December 2024.

legal_and_integrity.text: Sued then Liberal leader John Pesutto for defamation over his statements about her.
legal_and_integrity.outcome: The Federal Court found in her favour in December 2024 and awarded her $300,000 damages.

summary.text: Roshena Campbell, a barrister and Deputy Lord Mayor of Melbourne, heads the Liberal ticket for Western Metropolitan Region in the 2026 Legislative Council election.
